cards.text: Jesus is sitting on the Mount of Olives, and His disciples have asked Him privately when these things will happen and what the sign of His coming will be. He's been telling them what to watch for. Now He gets to the WHEN.

cards.question: The disciples want to know when Jesus is coming. Who does Jesus say knows that day or hour?

cards.text: Not the angels, not even the Son, only the Father. When the angel invited me here I asked him for the date, got the same answer, and this oven has been preheating EVER since.
Then Jesus reaches way back in history for a comparison: the days before the flood.

cards.question: Jesus compares His coming to a time long ago: 'As it was in the days of ___, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.'
What were people busy doing in the days before the flood, right up to the day Noah entered the ark?
True or false: the people before the flood saw it coming and got ready.

cards.text: They were oblivious until the flood came and swept them all away. Then that line again: 'So will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.'
Then Jesus paints a plain, everyday picture: two men out in the field.

cards.question: Two men are in the field. What does Jesus say happens to them?
True or false: Jesus gives the same picture with two women grinding at the mill.
Since nobody knows the day, Jesus tells His disciples, 'Therefore keep ___, because you do not know the day on which your Lord will come.'

cards.text: Then Jesus tells a quick story. Picture a homeowner who doesn't know which watch of the night a thief is coming.

cards.question: If the homeowner had known which watch of the night the thief was coming, what would he have done?
Jesus turns the homeowner story toward His disciples: 'For this reason, you also must be ___.'
True or false: Jesus says the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.

cards.text: That's the thing about thieves, friend. NOBODY ever got a message that said, 'Hey, swinging by around two, leave the porch light on.'
Then Jesus asks who the faithful and wise servant is. It's the one the master puts in charge of his household, to give the others their food at the proper time.

cards.question: The master returns and finds that servant doing his job. What does Jesus say about him?
True or false: the master puts the faithful servant in charge of all his possessions.

cards.text: Do the job, get put in charge of EVERYTHING the master owns. Friend, I stamped cookies faithfully for years, and my big promotion was the back of a junk drawer.
But then Jesus flips it. Suppose that servant is wicked.

cards.question: What does the wicked servant say in his heart about his master?

answers.text: My master will be away a long time
My master is coming back tonight
My master has forgotten about me

cards.text: Ah yes. The boss is out of town, and suddenly somebody's in the BIG chair with his feet up on the desk.

cards.question: True or false: while the master is away, the wicked servant keeps giving the others their food on time.
Instead, the wicked servant begins to ___ his fellow servants and to eat and drink with ___.
The wicked servant thinks his master will be gone a long time. When does the master come back?

answers.text: On a day he does not expect

cards.question: The master cuts the wicked servant to pieces and assigns him a place with the ___.

cards.text: It's a place where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Jesus is dead serious here, friend, and His teaching on the Mount of Olives isn't done yet.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage, and it reaches back to 24:43 after verse 44 has already been asked. The thief joke should ride on a card that carries part of the passage, such as card 1, which sets up the homeowner and the thief.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card repeats 24:47, which card 3 just asked, and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The junk drawer joke should ride on a card that tells the next moment, such as card 5, which turns to the wicked servant.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about 24:48, which card 6 just asked. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke should ride on a card that carries the next moment.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question starts with 'Instead,' and card 8 has just established that the servant doesn't keep feeding the others. Together they rule out 'feed,' the only other verb that fits blank 1. That leaves 'beat' as the only possible pick for blank 1.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says the master cuts the servant to pieces, which rules out 'faithful' as the group he is placed with. That leaves only 'drunkards' as a real alternative to 'hypocrites.' Replace 'faithful' with a believable group that the setup doesn't rule out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Almost all the humor sits on separate joke-only cards (stop 1 card 3, stop 2 card 5, stop 3 cards 4 and 7). Meanwhile, the cards that carry the passage are flat narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 4, 8 and 9, stop 2 card 1, and stop 3 cards 1 and 5. His reactions and laughs should come up on the cards that tell the passage.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
